Subject: CAIQ scope edges + request for consolidated evidence passport

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — Orchid Bank's security team did a pre-scan of Redwood's CAIQ answers and we have two quick asks before we start a deeper technical review: 1) clarify the scope edges around cross-region caching and ephemeral KV residency, and 2) a single "evidence passport" bundle that maps each CAIQ control ID to the exact artifact and the internal owner we can contact during our audit.

Specifically, we're looking for: 
- A short note on which controls are affected by your autoscaling fallback (model-variant fallback -> does that change data in-flight routing?).
- Proof pointers for log preservation / runbook access for the runtime (sample runtime trace acceptable).
- A roster naming control owners (team + email) for anything in the data-handling category.

Target: can you provide the passport (manifest + owner roster + 1 sample runtime log) by end-of-week (Dec 11)? If you can't meet that deadline, please propose an alternate date and a 30-minute sync.

We prefer a single package (zip or shared Drive folder) with a short manifest file so our auditors can navigate quickly.

Thanks — Marta
Marta Alvarez
Senior Information Security Manager
Orchid Bank

Hi Marta / Sofia,

Attached are the initial artifacts for the "evidence passport". This is v1 — we'll iterate after your review.

Attachments included:
- RI_CAIQ_evidence_manifest_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — a control-by-control manifest. For each CAIQ control we list: short summary, artifact type, artifact file/name, owner, and a confidence flag (sampled / full).
- control_owner_roster.csv — flat roster of owners for routing questions.
- log-sample-runtime-trace.txt — redacted token-level runtime trace showing request/response correlation IDs (timestamps scrubbed to date-only).

A couple of notes on scope edges you asked about:
- Autoscaling fallback: when we trigger model-variant fallback for capacity reasons, request routing remains within the same region and within the customer's configured residency boundary. We do not replicate customer inputs to other regions as part of fallback; we instead route to a compatible model variant in the same region or a pre-approved failover pool. We'll include a short diagram in the Drive folder.
- KV/prefix caching: prefix/KV caches are held on the serving node and are ephemeral; we include cache eviction policy and retention notes in the manifest.

If you'd like, we can redline the manifest to mark high-priority controls for your audit team.

Kimberly Park
Security Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

1) Could Redwood add a single-line explanation for controls that reference "ephemeral caches" vs persistent stores (so our auditors know which artifacts to request)?
2) Please confirm whether any of the attachments contain unredacted customer identifiers (we assume no; confirm for the log sample).

If you can reply with those two clarifications in-line, we can mark JIRA-SEC-4321 as ready for audit ingestion and schedule a 30-min hangout next week if needed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Marta
